title: Why clients don't step up
objectives: Name the five behaviours that stop clients from stepping up.
Give the compliant response to each.
body_md:
Most clients agree a step-up makes sense, then never do it. Make it automatic, small and tied to a raise.

| Behaviour | What it sounds like | What to say |
|---|---|---|
| Lifestyle creep | "The raise just disappeared." | "Let's send a slice of every raise to the SIP before it reaches your account." |
| Present bias | "I'll increase it next year." | "Set it now and it happens on its own. Waiting five years cost about ₹54 lakh in our example." |
| Fear of commitment | "What if I can't afford it later?" | "We'll set a cap, and it can be paused or reduced at review." |
| Anchoring on the start amount | "₹10,000 is my SIP." | "That was right five years ago. As a share of your income, it's now much smaller." |
| Waiting for markets | "I'll step up after the market settles." | "A step-up is about your income, not the market. Falls are good months to buy more units." |

**The one line to remember:** save more tomorrow, automatically.
example: Sameer has delayed for three years. Setting an automatic 5% step-up with a cap, timed to his April raise, removes the annual decision that he keeps postponing.
say: We'll send a slice of every raise to the SIP before it reaches your account.
A step-up is about your income, not the market.
never: Let's wait until the market settles.
You'll increase it when you feel ready.

talk_track.title: Why clients don't step up, and what to say
talk_track.text: Most clients agree a step-up makes sense, then never do it. Lifestyle creep: “the raise just disappeared”. Suggest sending a slice of every raise to the SIP first, before it reaches their account. Present bias: “I'll increase it next year”. Set it now, and it happens on its own. Fear of commitment: set a cap, and remind them it can be paused or reduced. Anchoring: ten thousand is much smaller as a share of income now. And waiting for markets: a step-up is about income, not the market.

check.q: A client says, "I'll increase it next year." What is the best response?
o: Set it now so it happens automatically, and mention the cost of a five-year delay
Stop the SIP until next year
check.why: Present bias is beaten by automation, not by good intentions.

check.q: A client says, "What if I can't afford it later?" What helps?
o: A promise that income will grow
A cap, plus the option to pause or reduce at review
check.why: A bounded commitment is easier to accept, and it can be revisited every year.

check.q: A client wants to wait for the market to settle before stepping up. What do you say?
o: A step-up is about your income, not the market; falls are good months to buy more units
Let's stop the SIP until then
check.why: The step-up decision is tied to income. Market timing is not part of it.
